questions.question: [NEET 2021 | Biology] Which is NOT a natural method of contraception?
questions.solution: # Answer: **(D) Cu-T** ## Explanation: **Natural Methods of Contraception** rely on biological processes or behavioral practices without using any artificial devices or chemicals: | Method | Type | How it works | |--------|------|-------------| | **Lactational amenorrhoea** | Natural \u₂₇₁₃ | Breastfeeding suppresses ovulation | | **Coitus interruptus** | Natural \u₂₇₁₃ | Withdrawal before ejaculation | | **Periodic abstinence** | Natural \u₂₇₁₃ | Avoiding intercourse during fertile days (ovulation window) | | **Cu-T** | **Artificial \u₂₇₁₇** | Mechanical device inserted in uterus | ## Why Cu-T is NOT Natural: - **Cu-T (Copper-T)** is an **Intrauterine Device (IUD)** - a physical object placed inside the uterus - It prevents implantation through the copper ions released - It's a **contraceptive device**, not a natural method ## Key Point to Remember: **Natural Contraceptive Methods:** - Lactational amenorrhoea - Periodic abstinence (Rhythm method/Safe period) - Coitus interruptus (Withdrawal method) **Artificial Methods Include:** - Barrier methods (condoms, diaphragm) - Hormonal methods (pills, injections) - IUDs (Cu-T, IUCd) - Permanent methods (tubectomy, vasectomy)

questions.question: [NEET 2023 | Biology] In IVF (In Vitro Fertilisation), the embryo is transferred to the uterus at what stage?
questions.solution: ## Answer: **(C) Blastocyst stage** --- ## Step-by-Step Explanation: ### Why Blastocyst Stage is Correct: 1. **Developmental Readiness** - The blastocyst is a fluid-filled structure with 100-150 cells - It has differentiated into two cell types: - **Trophoblast** (outer layer) \u₂₁₉₂ forms placenta - **Inner Cell Mass** (ICM) \u₂₁₉₂ forms embryo 2. **Natural Timing** - In natural conception, the embryo reaches the blastocyst stage on Day 5-6 - This is exactly when it naturally enters the uterus for implantation - Transferring at this stage mimics natural physiology 3. **Clinical Success** - Highest implantation rates ( 50-60%) compared to earlier stages - Better uterine receptivity at this stage - Reduces ectopic pregnancy risk --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong: | Stage | Why NOT Used | Problem | |-------|--------------|---------| | **(A) Zygote** | Too early | Not yet cleaved; embryo is still in fallopian tube naturally | | **(B) 8-cell** | Premature | Less implantation competence; poor success rates | | **(D) Morula** | Suboptimal | Transitional stage; not yet fully differentiated like blastocyst | --- ## Key Fact to Remember: \U₀₀₀₁f₄cc **"Blastocyst on Day 5-6 in IVF matches natural embryo timing in the uterus"** Modern IVF protocols prefer **blastocyst stage transfer** because it achieves maximum implantation success by synchronizing with uterine receptivity.

They are used in the form of tablets and hence, are popularly called the pills. Pills have to be taken daily for a period of 21 days, starting preferably within the first five days of menstrual cycle. After a gap of 7 days (during which menstruation occurs) it has to be repeated in the same pattern till the female desires to prevent conception. They inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as alter the quality of cervical mucous to prevent/retard entry of sperms. Pills are very effective with lesser side effects and are well accepted by the females. Saheli the new oral contraceptive for the females contains a non-steroidal preparation.
